stories.stat_label: when she arrived at the shelter
stories.headline: A 70 lb bulldog who couldn't walk lost 20 lb and got adopted
stories.summary: Peggy Sue was so heavy the RSPCA had to carry her in a crate. A foster carer slowly built up her walks, and she dropped from 32.5 kg to 23.5 kg before a family in Taunton took her home.
stories.why: Now she loves walks, car trips and splashing in streams.

stories.stat_label: years old, and still holding clues
stories.headline: 3,000-year-old cups in Jordan may hold traces of Indian pepper
stories.summary: Chemists tested 7 burial cups from a tomb at Pella holding at least 82 people. 3 contained piperine, the compound in black pepper, a spice from India's Western Ghats, hinting at long-distance trade.
stories.why: The cups were dug up in 1987. Their walls kept the secret for decades.

stories.headline: Steam could replace toxic chemicals on strawberry farms
stories.summary: UC Santa Cruz researchers injected steam into strawberry beds to kill soil fungi, bacteria and weeds before planting. Farmers in the 4-farm trial reported bigger, healthier plants and more fruit.
stories.why: Organic growers finally get a way to protect crops without fumigants.

stories.stat_label: the year people saw it explode
stories.headline: A star exploded in 1181, and it's still alive
stories.summary: Astronomers in Japan, China and the Arab world recorded a new light in 1181. Now Gemini North shows its remnant, Pa 30, in sharp detail, with the star that survived the blast sitting right at its centre.
stories.why: It's the only known star in our galaxy to survive this type of explosion.

fun_fact: The 1181 supernova stayed visible in the night sky for at least 185 days.
